title: The Unexpected Visitor
description: Practise the past continuous and past simple, then write a story about a surprising visitor.
instructions: Do the exercises in Part 1. Then write your text in Part 2.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: I ___ my homework when somebody knocked on the door.
exercises.explanation: Use the past continuous for a longer action in progress and the past simple for the short action that interrupts it.

exercises.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.text: It ___ (rain) heavily, so the street was empty.
exercises.explanation: Use the past continuous (was/were + -ing) to describe the background of a story.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
answers: The man who stood at the door was completely wet.
exercises.explanation: A relative clause with "who" comes straight after the person it describes: the man who stood at the door.

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: He opened his bag and taked out an old photograph.
answers: He opened his bag and took out an old photograph.
exercises.explanation: "Take" is irregular. Its past simple form is "took", not "taked".

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: ___ I didn't know him, he seemed strangely familiar.
exercises.explanation: "Although" joins two contrasting ideas in one sentence: Although I didn't know him, he seemed familiar.

exercises.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.text: When I opened the door, a tall man ___ (smile) at me.
exercises.explanation: Use the past simple for a series of completed actions in a story: I opened, he smiled.

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: While we were talk, the lights suddenly went out.
answers: While we were talking, the lights suddenly went out.
exercises.explanation: The past continuous is was/were + the -ing form: we were talking.

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word WHILE. Begin: "The doorbell rang ..."
exercises.text: I was cooking dinner. The doorbell rang.
answers: The doorbell rang while I was cooking dinner.
While I was cooking dinner, the doorbell rang.
exercises.explanation: "While" introduces the longer action in the past continuous: The doorbell rang while I was cooking dinner.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: The man said he ___ live in our house many years ago.
exercises.explanation: Use "used to + infinitive" for a past situation that is not true now.

exercises.prompt: Write the correct form of the word in brackets.
exercises.text: To my ___ (amaze), he knew my name.
exercises.explanation: After "my" we need a noun. Add -ment to make a noun: amaze - amazement.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
answers: It turned out that he was my uncle.
exercises.explanation: "It turned out that ..." means we discovered something surprising later.

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: He looked more old than my grandfather.
answers: He looked older than my grandfather.
exercises.explanation: Short adjectives take -er in the comparative: old - older.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: He showed me a photo of a girl ___ face looked just like mine.
exercises.explanation: Use "whose" + noun to show possession: a girl whose face (= her face).

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word HAD. Begin: "He ..."
exercises.text: It was necessary for him to leave before midnight.
answers: He had to leave before midnight.
exercises.explanation: Use "had to + infinitive" for something that was necessary in the past.

exercises.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.text: He suddenly stopped ___ (talk) and looked out of the window.
exercises.explanation: "Stop + -ing" means an activity ends: he stopped talking.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.explanation: Use the present perfect with "since" for a situation that started in the past and continues now.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
answers: I asked him who he was.
exercises.explanation: In reported or indirect questions, the word order is like a statement: who he was (not "who was he").

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: If I knew who he was, I will tell you.
answers: If I knew who he was, I would tell you.
exercises.explanation: In the second conditional, use "would" (not "will") with the past simple after "if".

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word WHICH. Begin: "He gave me a box ..."
exercises.text: He gave me a box. It was full of old letters.
answers: He gave me a box which was full of old letters.
exercises.explanation: Use "which" to join two sentences about the same thing: a box which was full of ...

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word TOO. Begin: "I was ..."
exercises.text: I was so frightened that I couldn't say anything.
answers: I was too frightened to say anything.
exercises.explanation: "So ... that I couldn't" can be changed to "too + adjective + to-infinitive".

task.prompt: Write a story that begins with this sentence: "It was a cold winter evening when somebody knocked on the door."
contentPoints: Give the story a surprising or interesting ending.
usefulLanguage: It was a cold winter evening when ...
task.modelAnswer:
It was a cold winter evening when somebody knocked on the door. I was watching TV alone because my parents were visiting my aunt.

When I opened the door, I saw an old man who was wearing a long brown coat. He was holding an umbrella, but he was completely wet. "I'm sorry to disturb you," he said. "I lived in this house sixty years ago. May I look at the garden?"

At first, I felt nervous. However, he looked kind, so I took him to the back door. He walked to the old apple tree, dug a little with his hands and found a small metal box.

Inside, there was a photograph of a young girl. "My sister," he whispered, and his eyes filled with tears. Then he thanked me and disappeared into the rain.
